ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA, S.C. 2000, c. 17) and FINTRAC Beneficial Ownership Reporting requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Articles of Incorporation or Partnership Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against FINTRAC, OFAC SDN, UN Sanctions lists, and domestic CRA sanctions; full KYC and beneficial ownership verification

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry (BC Registry Services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Strict adherence to English language; no transliteration required; names must use Latin alphabet
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, applicant may file a written appeal to the Registrar within 30 days; appeal involves administrative review and possible hearing; decision is final unless judicial review

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for Limited Partnerships provided the registered office is a valid physical or virtual address accepted by BC Registry Services; must not be a mailbox only
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (under 5%) for unannounced inspections on new Limited Partnerships; inspections are conducted on a risk basis by BC Registry Services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and name search fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for corporate incorporation services in British Columbia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC Registry Services filing fee for Limited Partnership
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under BC Business Corporations Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and mailing address setup
Hague Apostille and document legalization (if foreign documents required)
UBO and AML compliance documentation preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly rate for AML due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 62-86; Partnership Regulation, BC Reg. 414/2001; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 applicable only to corporate GPs
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) and issuance of Certificate of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital. At least one general partner with unlimited liability and one limited partner required; limited partners must contribute money or property as stated in the registration, without cash escrow requirement under BC law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner (i) adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement of Surgical Laparoscopy Towers LP; (ii) directs registration of the Partnership under the Partnership Act (British Columbia) with the Registrar of Companies; (iii) establishes the registered office at [address], British Columbia; (iv) appoints [Name] as Managing General Partner and [Name] as Corporate Secretary; (v) authorizes the appointed officers to execute statutory filings, open banking accounts, secure the Medical Device Establishment Licence, and obtain all municipal, environmental, and occupational permits; and (vi) authorizes expenditures of capital contributions for formation, licensing, and initial operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Name Requests Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a NUANS name search request through the BC Registries online portal, selecting a distinct name containing 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP'; pay the name reservation fee and submit the automated NUANS report with the reservation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new name reservation with revised distinctive elements; correctness amendments may be made within 30 days without additional search fee if registry error is established

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary public in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement identifying general and limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management authority of the general partner, and restrictions on limited partner participation; ensure execution in counterparts and witnessed signatures
required_dossiers: Statement of capital contributions and realization dates
Consent of general partner to act
Consent of limited partners to be bound
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is identified, amend the agreement by supplementary deed or restatement; no registry filing is required unless statutory information changes

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) online, attach the name reservation and executed agreement extracts, list full name and address of each general and limited partner, and pay the registration fee; upon approval the Registrar issues the Certificate of Limited Partnership
required_dossiers: Form LP-1 Application for Registration of Limited Partnership
Registered office address and records office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, respond within 30 days to the Notice of Intention to Reject; correct and resubmit the form with an accompanying statutory declaration; filing fee is refunded if the registry rejects the application

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership for a federal Business Number and open CRA accounts for GST/HST (accounting on accrual basis), payroll deductions if employees are hired, and import/export (RM) account for medical device components; use the Certificate of Limited Partnership as identification
required_dossiers: General partner's identification and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or rejected, call the CRA Business Number hotline or resubmit online; discrepancies in entity type can be cured by filing Form RC1-WP and attaching the BC certificate clarifying partnership status

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Ministry of Finance, Provincial Sales Tax; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership for Provincial Sales Tax (PST) through the BC Taxpayer Portal, and create a WorkSafeBC account for mandatory occupational injury insurance if the partnership will have employees; provide the partnership's Business Number and NAICS code 339112
required_dossiers: Estimated payroll information for WorkSafeBC classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the PST account online if business activity codes are misclassified; for WorkSafeBC reclassification, file an Application for Reconsideration on the Business Classification within 30 days

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local government / municipality where registered office and manufacturing facility are located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the manufacturing occupancy, confirming zoning for light industrial/medical device production, and obtain an occupancy permit following building inspection; submit the partnership registration certificate and site plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning denies the use, apply for a minor variance or temporary use permit; if building code deficiencies are cited, complete remedial construction and schedule a re-inspection before licence issuance

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada, Medical Devices Directorate (Medical Devices Bureau)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act, RSC 1985, c. F-27 and Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier under the Waste Discharge Regulation of the Environmental Management Act, SBC 2003, c. 53; full EIA report not typically mandated for moderate-scale medical device assembly, but triggered if discharge thresholds exceed Schedule 1 limits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge per municipal sewer bylaw and EMA effluent quality criteria; VOC emission controls under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, SC 1999, c. 33 and the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation, BC Reg. 261/2016 for solvents and cleaning agents

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire authority under the BC Fire Code; structural load inspection and occupancy permit from the municipal building department; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance under the Workers Compensation Act, RSBC 1996, c. 492, including HRMS-compliant electrical safety for high-power endoscopy tower testing

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online, GST/HST accounts, and income tax administration; British Columbia Ministry of Finance — PST registration via BC eTaxBC (https://www.etax.gov.bc.ca/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership registers for a Canadian Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account through CRA's Business Registration Online or by submitting Form RC1 / RC151. The partnership must provide its partnership agreement, proof of foreign registration, Canadian contact/agent information, and details of anticipated Canadian sales. After obtaining the BN and GST/HST registration, the LP must separately register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST through the provincial online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada), a limited partnership is fiscally transparent; income, losses, and credits flow through to partners. For GST/HST purposes, the limited partnership is treated as a separate 'person' and may register as a GST/HST registrant. Territorial scope: Canadian-source income is allocated to resident and non-resident partners; non-resident partners are taxable only on Canadian-source income, subject to treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide check-the-box entity elections; partnerships are transparent by default. Available statutory elections include an elected fiscal period for partnerships under ITA s. 249.1(4), a section 216 election for non-residents with Canadian rental income, and GST/HST joint elections under ETA s. 156 for closely related corporations. Hybrid mismatch deductibility is restricted by ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.3 where a payment is deductible in Canada but treated as non-includible by the payee jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7% as a separate retail sales tax; BC uses the 5% GST and 7% PST uncombined (no HST in BC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in total taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in the current and preceding three consecutive calendar quarters, or across a single calendar quarter for small supplier status; BC PST: CAD 10,000 in gross taxable sales in the immediately preceding 12 months (small seller exemption).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada and British Columbia do not mandate real-time electronic invoicing clearance, API-based fiscal stamping, or a central clearance platform for GST/HST or PST. Suppliers may issue paper or electronic invoices; CRA accepts electronic records if they remain readable and auditable. No digital stamping or continuous transaction control framework applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods (including ultra-HD 4K minimally invasive endoscopy towers classified under ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339112) is zero-rated to 0% GST/HST if the supplier exports the goods, or ships them at the direction of the recipient, to a destination outside Canada. Services and intangibles may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not using or consuming them in Canada. PST does not apply to goods delivered outside Canada under a contract of sale where the seller ships to an export destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export documentation and proof of physical export
Commercial invoice and supply contract describing the goods as manufactured medical devices
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess an export zero-rating claim within the normal four-year reassessment period; where misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default is established, reassessment is not time-limited. A zero-rating claim that fails substantiation exposes the taxpayer to reassessment at 5% GST plus applicable BC PST, interest, and a 25% false-statement or omission penalty under ETA s. 285(1). BC PST officials may impose a 75% penalty for wilful evasion or attempt to evade tax. Criminal prosecution can result in fines and imprisonment. Retrospective clawback of exported refunds and input tax credits is available where the 180-day foreign exchange repatriation or documentary requirement is not met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime under the Bank of Canada Act. Current account transactions are freely convertible without prior approval. Capital account transactions, including profit remittances, dividends, and interest, are generally permitted but require prior notification or approval from the Bank of Canada for amounts exceeding prescribed thresholds; profit remittance is unrestricted for Canadian residents subject to tax reporting and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign exchange proceeds or convert them freely at market rates. All foreign exchange transactions must be reported to the Bank of Canada (via authorized dealers) and to the Canada Revenue Agency for tax compliance; recommended repatriation timeline is 30-90 days for operational accounting purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs; platforms such as Wise or Stripe are usable for cross-border payments but subject to FINTRAC registration, OSFI oversight, and strict AML/KYC requirements. Full EMI licensing for non-residents is prohibited; cross-border digital issuance remains constrained by provincial and federal regulatory frameworks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for directors, authorized signers, and KYC interviews for new Limited Partnership accounts in British Columbia. Remote or video-based opening is permitted only for existing clients or under FINTRAC exceptions; in-person verification is required for all new corporate entities to satisfy anti-money laundering standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership or source of funds for capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited Partnership agreement, certificate of formation, director resolutions, proof of address, beneficial ownership statements, and source-of-funds documentation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction connections or unexplained wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence package including source-of-wealth evidence, transaction purpose letters, and independent verification reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via SWIFT wire transfers using purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INVESTMENT'. Verification requires matching beneficiary details against account-opening documents, tax identification numbers, and beneficial ownership records; correspondent banking relationships with Canadian Tier-1 institutions ensure efficient processing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through domestic banks. All disbursements must comply with export controls, Incoterms, and proper invoicing; purpose codes such as 'TRADE PAYMENT' are required for regulatory reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two (2) months after each registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration defaults; after two consecutive missed annual reports, the Registrar may cancel the limited partnership registration, resulting in strike-off/dissolution and loss of limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Limited Partnership Transparency Register Annual Declaration (embedded in Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Furnished concurrently with the BC Limited Partnership Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or declare compliance with the transparency register requirement may result in administrative penalties and restrictions on disposition of real property under the Land Owner Transparency Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 fiscal period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$25 per day, up to C$2,500 per return under Income Tax Act section 162(7); gross-negligence penalty applies in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (if the LP is a GST/HST registrant annual filer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 1% of the net amount owing plus 25% of that base penalty per full month up to four months; daily interest accrues on unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) Vendor Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Consumer Taxation Branch, British Columbia Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: As assigned by the Ministry; generally within three (3) months after the vendor's fiscal year-end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at prime plus three (3) percentage points on late remittance; late-filing penalties and escalating administrative sanctions apply for repeated non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue/asset-based compulsory audit thresholds apply to a British Columbia limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Act. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only where: (i) the LP is a reporting issuer or investment fund under securities legislation; (ii) the partnership agreement or a lender/covenant requires an audit; or (iii) a court or the Registrar orders an audit under investigative powers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP per the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for qualifying private entities; the LP may adopt ASPE unless the partnership agreement or external stakeholders require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BC Limited Partnership Act, the LP must establish and maintain a transparency register of individuals with significant control (ISC). On every annual report filing, the general partner must confirm in writing that the transparency register has been prepared, retained, and updated to reflect all ownership and control changes during the preceding year. There is no separate UBO filing; the confirmation is a declaration embedded in the annual report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book of General Partner Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$110 – US$550 typical annual registered office/agent retainer for a BC limited partnership
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$14,000 – US$55,000 typical certified audit fee for a mid-sized medical device manufacturing LP under ASPE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Manufacturing and Processing (M&P) deduction reduces federal rate to 13% for qualifying activities; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credits; BC provincial tax credits for manufacturing and innovation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Statement of Partnership Income) filed via CRA's electronic filing system (EFTP or NETFILE)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (gross revenue from manufacturing and sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income earned in Canada; non-resident partners must include their share in their home jurisdiction and may claim treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business expenses (cost of goods sold, operating expenses, depreciation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be reasonable and supported by documentation; non-resident partners cannot claim expenses not incurred in Canada.
Allocate net income to partners based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding on distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to each partner (name, address, SIN/BN, share percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full details for non-resident partners; the partnership must withhold 25% on distributions unless treaty reduces the rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $25 per day per partner (max $2,500); additional penalties for failure to provide information, plus interest on any unpaid amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners; not a dividend but a partnership distribution)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident partner must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) and file Form NR-301 (or NR-302) with the CRA. The partnership must also file Form NR-4 (Return of Amounts Paid or Credited to Non-Residents) to report distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 10% (e.g., US) or 0% (e.g., certain treaties); Interest: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 0% (e.g., US) or 10% (e.g., some treaties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods; CAD 500,000 for services, interest, royalties, and other transactions with each non-resident
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies the OECD economic substance requirements; the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) can recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance. For a limited partnership, the CRA may scrutinize the allocation of income and the existence of real business activity, especially in manufacturing operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting income, inflating expenses, or misrepresenting the partnership's financial position to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (s. 239); fines up to 200% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors (general partners) may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in the evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a limited partnership without real business activity, employees, or physical presence, solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR may deny tax benefits; penalties up to 50% of the tax benefit; CRA may reassess and impose interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be held personally liable for the partnership's tax liabilities if the partnership is deemed a sham; limited partners may lose limited liability if they participate in management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement a compliance program, report suspicious transactions, or verify client identity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 for corporations; criminal penalties for individuals; potential seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly failed to comply; travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years for criminal offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions, resulting in understated income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments to income, penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (if documentation incomplete), and interest on reassessed amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they signed false statements or knowingly participated in the mispricing; civil restitution and potential criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not filing the T5013 or other required returns by the statutory deadline, or failing to provide partner information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty of $25 per day per partner (max $2,500); additional penalties for failure to provide information; interest on any unpaid amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be personally liable for penalties if they were responsible for filing and failed to do so; CRA may issue a director's liability assessment.
